query: Why do some incidents take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: The type of incident (email, database, vpn) is a characteristic of the incident, not a constitutive part of the REASON it is delayed. It may correlate with delay but is not an aspect-of the delay cause itself.

per_column.name: failure_pattern
per_column.rationale: Describes the nature of the technical failure (connection_failure, service_down). This characterizes the incident, not the delay mechanism; it is a predictor of resolution time, not a facet of the delay reason.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Blast radius (individual_user vs outage_wide) is an attribute of the incident's impact; it may influence delay but is not a constitutive part of the delay reason.

per_column.name: assignment_lag
per_column.rationale: Delay incurred at the assignment/triage stage (multi_day, unassigned) is directly a constitutive part of why resolution takes longer -- a genuine facet of delay.

per_column.name: assignee_workload_signal
per_column.rationale: Resource/capacity contention (high_volume_assignee) is a constitutive aspect of delay causation arising from the handling process, an 'aspect of' why work stalls.

per_column.name: reassignment_indicator
per_column.rationale: Ping-ponging/rerouting of tickets is a process-level constitutive contributor to delay, a legitimate facet of the delay concept.

per_column.name: remote_context
per_column.rationale: Whether the incident is remote-related is contextual metadata about the incident, not a constitutive part of the delay reason.

per_column.name: caller_repeat_reporter
per_column.rationale: A single-valued (all true=500) attribute about the caller; it carries no discriminating information and is not a part-of the delay concept.

per_column.name: incident_is_open_unresolved
per_column.rationale: Whether the incident is still open/unresolved restates the outcome (long resolution) itself rather than decomposing its causes; it is a restatement of the whole, not a facet.

judge.rationale: Only three columns (assignment_lag, assignment/workload, reassignment) are genuine constitutive facets of 'incident_delay_reasons' -- they capture process-level contributors (triage lag, resource contention, rerouting) that are aspects-of the delay. The majority of columns are external predictors describing the incident's type, failure nature, scope, or context, which may correlate with delay but are not part-of the delay concept; one is a restatement of the outcome and one is degenerate/irrelevant. Among the real facets, assignment_lag and assignee_workload_signal partially overlap (both reflect handling-stage capacity/queuing and share an 'unassigned' bucket), lowering mutual exclusivity. Exhaustiveness is weak: major delay facets such as vendor/third-party wait, awaiting-customer/pending time, diagnosis/complexity effort, and SLA/priority-driven queuing are not represented.
